note: One [[errata.field]] name correction whose expected_records name one member with two complete original alternatives (column ANSWER named GenericVar, and PHYSICAL named 'Physical name', which supplies the replacement). This file authors them PHYSICAL first; its twin errata-field-record-alternatives-load-in-one-order authors them in the other order. Both load the alternatives in one canonical order (by projection token, the order `capture_expectations` emits), so the two `loads` projections are identical: authored order is never evidence, and a projection change that reorders tokens (the dropped code-set references did) cannot stale an entry whose originals are unchanged. The order shown is the canonical one; the claim is that both cases show the same.
fails_if: `RecordExpectation` (source_curation.py) keeps the authored order of `alternatives` instead of sorting them by projection token, so this file and its twin load the alternatives in different orders and compiled guards compare them unequal to the captured originals
